docs.text: Job Application Assistant A sophisticated multi-agent job application automation system built on Google's Agent Development Kit (ADK). This system automates the complete job application workflow: scraping jobs from multiple sites, creating Google Drive folders with resumes, generating tailored cover letters, and submitting applications. 🏗️ System Architecture User Input → Orchestrator Agent → Specialized Sub-Agents → Database & Google Drive Agent Hierarchy orchestrator_agent (LlmAgent) ├── job_scraper_agent (scrapes from 5+ sites) ├── resource_manager_agent (creates folders, copies resumes) │ └── batch_resource_manager (handles bulk folder operations) ├── content_generator_agent (analyzes fit, writes cover letters) │ └── batch_content_generator (handles >25 jobs with rate limiting) ├── database_agent (database operations) ├── application_submitter_agent (automated submissions) │ └── batch_submitter (sequential job applications) └── email_assistant_agent (email classification) 🔑 Key Features Multi-Site Job Scraping : LinkedIn, Indeed, Glassdoor, ZipRecruiter, Google Jobs Smart Deduplication : Prevents duplicate applications across sites Chrome Extension : Manual job saving from any website with one-click integration Google Drive Integration : Automated folder creation and document management AI Content Generation : Personalized cover letters using Gemini models And Resumes Browser Automation : Headless job application submission with CAPTCHA solving Email Classification : Process job-related emails automatically Batch Processing : Handle large volumes with rate limiting 📚 Documentation Master Overview - Comprehensive system documentation Chrome Extension Guide - Extension setup Agent-specific documentation in each sub-agent folder

docs.text: Job Application Assistant Chrome Extension 🚀 Quick Start Loading the Extension in Chrome Open Chrome and navigate to chrome://extensions/ Enable "Developer mode" (toggle in top right) Click "Load unpacked" Select the chrome-extension/dist folder The extension icon (JA) should appear in your toolbar! Testing the Extension Visit a job listing on: LinkedIn (e.g., linkedin.com/jobs/view/...) Indeed (e.g., indeed.com/viewjob?...) Glassdoor ZipRecruiter Click the extension icon - you should see: "On Job Page" indicator Current job details extracted Save Job button Click "Save Job" to save it locally 🔧 Development Setup npm install Development Mode (with hot reload) npm run dev Production Build npm run build 📁 Project Structure chrome-extension/ ├── dist/ # Built extension (load this in Chrome) ├── src/ │ ├── popup/ # Extension popup UI │ ├── content/ # Content scripts for job extraction │ └── background/ # Service worker for API calls ├── manifest.json # Extension configuration └── webpack.config.js # Build configuration ✅ Chrome extension structure with Manifest V3 ✅ Job extraction for LinkedIn, Indeed, Glassdoor, ZipRecruiter ✅ Popup UI with job saving functionality ✅ Local storage for saved jobs ✅ Multi-site support with site-specific parsers

docs.text: Setting Up the Public Documentation Repository Step 1: Create the Public Repo Go to https://github.com/new Create a new repository: Name: job-application-assistant-docs Description: "Documentation for Job Application Assistant" Public (important!) DO NOT initialize with README, .gitignore, or license Click "Create repository" Step 2: Generate Deploy Keys Run these commands in your terminal: cd /home/dave/Desktop/job_application_assitant/docs-config # Generate the deploy key pair (no passphrase - just press Enter twice) ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f job-docs-deploy-key -C "davidbzyk@gmail.com" Step 3: Add Keys to GitHub Add Public Key to Public Repo: Go to your new job-application-assistant-docs repo Settings → Deploy keys → Add deploy key Title: "Docs Deploy Key" Key: Copy contents of job-docs-deploy-key.pub Check "Allow write access" Add key Add Private Key to Private Repo: Go to your private job_application_assistant repo Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions New repository secret Name: ACTIONS_DEPLOY_KEY Value: Copy contents of job-docs-deploy-key (no .pub) Add secret Step 4: Set Up GitHub Actions Create the workflow directory and copy the deploy file: mkdir -p /home/dave/Desktop/job_application_assitant/.github/workflows cp /home/dave/Desktop/job_application_assitant/docs-config/deploy-docs.yml /home/dave/Desktop/job_application_assitant/.github/workflows/ Step 5: Update the Workflow Edit .github/workflows/deploy-docs.yml and update line 44 to use your GitHub username: git clone git@github.com:YOUR_GITHUB_USERNAME/job-application-assistant-docs.git docs-public Step 6: Enable GitHub Pages on Public Repo Go to the public job-application-assistant-docs repo Settings → Pages Source: Deploy from a branch Branch: gh-pages (will be created automatically) Folder: / (root) Save Step 7: Commit and Push cd /home/dave/Desktop/job_application_assitant git add .github/workflows/deploy-docs.yml git add docs-config/ git add README.md git commit -m "feat: Add MkDocs documentation setup" git push That's it! The GitHub Action will: 1. Trigger on push to main 2. Build the docs using MkDocs 3. Push to the public repo 4. GitHub Pages will serve them at: https://YOUR_USERNAME.github.io/job-application-assistant-docs/ Note on Updates The workflow only triggers when these files change: - Any README.md file - Files in docs-config/ - Files in ai-docs/ - The workflow file itself This prevents unnecessary builds.
